content: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors are medications used to treat congestive heart failure in pediatric patients. These drugs work by blocking the angiotensin-converting enzyme, which plays a key role in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. By inhibiting this enzyme, the medications reduce the production of angiotensin II, a substance that causes blood vessels to constrict. This leads to vasodilation, or the widening of blood vessels, which decreases the workload on the heart. Additionally, these inhibitors help reduce fluid retention by lowering aldosterone levels, which can improve symptoms of heart failure in children.
